findings.title: An order could be marked PAID for any payment_id in the request body
findings.description: Carried from the baseline review, finding 1. createOrder trusted the body’s payment_id; fixed so payment-service must confirm the payment (completed, this buyer, full total, not used for another order).
findings.root_cause: The order path trusted a client-supplied payment reference.
findings.technical_impact: Order state could advance without a completed payment (C-47 Invariant #2).
findings.business_impact: Goods could be released unpaid; seller payouts recorded against nothing.
findings.recommendation: None — closed. P6 re-traces the order → payment flow end to end.
acceptance_criteria: P6 traces a Mode-2 purchase and finds the order PAID only after payment-service confirms it

findings.title: Dependencies with known advisories remain in four Express services, payment-service and two apps
findings.description: Carried from the baseline review, finding 2. Closed for 22 apps (Next 15.5.29) and 15 Fastify services (Nest 11 / Fastify 5). Still open on main: gateway · auth · wallet · realtime on Express 4 / Nest 10; payment-service’s @stellar/stellar-sdk major; zod 4. P0 confirms tec-nbf and tec-brookfield main still pin next 15.5.12 (their PRs #32 · #28 are open, not merged).

evidence.observation: tec-nbf and tec-brookfield: dependencies.next = 15.5.12 on origin/main

findings.root_cause: Upgrades were done in batches; the Express services and two late-joining apps were not in the batch.
findings.technical_impact: Known-vulnerable framework versions run in production.
findings.business_impact: Exposure to published exploits on public endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Merge NBF #32 and Brookfield #28; after 1 Dec, upgrade the four Express services and the stellar-sdk major.
acceptance_criteria: npm audit --omit=dev reports 0 critical / 0 high in every service and app (P3 records the run)

remediation.note: The two apps close with these merges; the four Express services and the stellar-sdk major are scheduled after 1 Dec (Actions minutes).

findings.title: Fastify internal-key guards tested the raw URL for /internal/
findings.description: Carried from the baseline review, finding 3. Fixed in all 16 copies; CI checks the copies are identical.
findings.technical_impact: An internal route reachable as a user call inside the network.
findings.business_impact: Not reachable from outside (the gateway decodes and refuses).

findings.title: The Hub's Content-Security-Policy still allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' scripts
findings.description: Carried from the baseline review, finding 4. connect-src was narrowed to named hosts (tec-app #324, closed). script-src still carries 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; the Pi SDK load path has to change first. The header is public, so this is not withheld.
findings.root_cause: The Pi SDK bootstrap relies on inline script.
findings.technical_impact: An injected script would not be blocked by CSP.
findings.business_impact: CSP gives no second line of defence against XSS on the payment hub.
findings.recommendation: Move the Pi SDK bootstrap to a nonce- or hash-allowed script, then drop 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval'.
acceptance_criteria: The Hub's production CSP header has no 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' in script-src
A Pi Browser sign-in and Mode-2 payment still work

remediation.note: Needs the Pi SDK bootstrap moved to a nonce'd script first; taken up in P3 (Run 2).

findings.title: Template fixes do not reach the apps made from it — the mechanism is not on main yet
findings.description: Carried from the baseline review, finding 5. The template-sync mechanism (manifest, check/apply script, weekly fleet-drift job) is built in tec-template-base #56, but P0 finds no template-sync.json on origin/main: until it merges, nothing reports drift.
findings.root_cause: Apps are copies of the template with no link back.
findings.technical_impact: Fixes made once are missing from some apps for weeks.
findings.business_impact: Uneven security and sign-in behaviour across the 24 apps.
findings.recommendation: Merge tec-template-base #56 and the 20 app PRs that adopt it.
acceptance_criteria: The first fleet-drift run lists no app as drifted, or opens one issue that names each

remediation.note: The mechanism exists; it is not on main yet.

findings.title: No staging environment, no alert on a failed backup, no uptime paging
findings.description: Carried from the baseline review, finding 6. Supabase can now be dumped by backup-job but waits on two variables. P8 verifies the runtime side.
findings.root_cause: Operations grew around one production environment.
findings.technical_impact: Failures are found by users, not by the platform.
findings.business_impact: An outage or a lost backup is noticed late.
findings.recommendation: Add an uptime monitor that pages; send backup failures to an alert channel; set the two Supabase backup variables.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberate backup failure produces an alert
Stopping a service pages within 5 minutes

remediation.note: Uptime paging, a backup alert channel and two Supabase variables are account-level settings; P8 verifies.

findings.title: Hand-written input validation in seven services; low coverage floors; very long Hub files
findings.description: Carried from the baseline review, finding 7 (the Ecommerce dead middleware part is closed). P2 measures this.
findings.root_cause: Services written before the shared validation pattern.
findings.technical_impact: Unvalidated edge cases reach the services.
findings.recommendation: P2 lists the services and files; remediation adopts zod at each edge.
acceptance_criteria: Every service validates request bodies with a schema library
No Hub source file over 600 lines without a recorded reason

remediation.note: Measured in P2 (Run 2), fixed against its list.

findings.title: One HS256 JWT secret is shared by 20 services and 24 apps
findings.description: Carried from the baseline review, finding 8. A leak of the secret anywhere forges any identity everywhere. One Redis is the whole event bus (P9/P10 assess).
findings.root_cause: Symmetric signing chosen early; every verifier holds the signing key.
findings.technical_impact: The blast radius of one leaked variable is the whole platform.
findings.business_impact: Account takeover of any user, admin included, from one leak.
findings.recommendation: Finish the rotation plan: asymmetric signing (the issuer alone holds the private key).
acceptance_criteria: Only tec-auth-service holds a signing key
Every verifier holds only a public key

remediation.note: Last step of the rotation plan (asymmetric signing); backend, after 1 Dec.

findings.title: The generated C-11 (repository map) and C-44 (environment variables) are stale against the code
findings.description: scripts/check-drift.py against every origin/main: 34 pass, 2 fail. C-11 is missing the current app versions (Next 15.5.29, tec-ui ^3.0.0 ranges); C-44 is missing LIFE_* variables now read by life-service and ai-service. The weekly drift job would report the same.
findings.root_cause: Code merged today without the generated docs being regenerated.
findings.technical_impact: The repository map this audit uses as a baseline lags the code.
findings.business_impact: Decisions read from C-11/C-44 use yesterday’s facts.
findings.recommendation: Run scripts/generate-code-docs.py --repos-dir … --ref origin/main and commit the result, after the open app PRs merge.

remediation.note: C-11 and C-44 regenerated from origin/main; check-drift.py 36 pass · 0 fail.

findings.title: A nested tec-core-backend/tec-core-backend/k6/ folder holds the load tests
findings.description: The only content of the nested folder is k6/; .github/workflows/load-test.yml runs it. The doubled name reads as an accidental copy and hides the load tests from anyone looking at the root.
findings.root_cause: A folder copied into itself at some point.
findings.technical_impact: Confusing layout; a cleanup could delete the load tests by mistake.
findings.recommendation: Move k6/ to the root (or tools/k6) and update load-test.yml in the same change.

remediation.note: k6/ moved to the root; load-test.yml updated. The branch is pushed without a PR, so no CI minutes are spent before 1 Dec.

findings.title: The port authority C-20 does not describe eight of the deployed services
findings.description: P0 counts 20 deployable services plus backup-job in tec-core-backend (and the shared library and service template). C-20, the backend-services and port authority, names 12. tec-business, tec-life, tec-nexus, tec-platform, tec-search and tec-trust-service and tec-backup-job do not appear in it at all; tec-ai and tec-connection-service appear once each. Those services start with PORT required (no default in main.ts). C-02 §1 names their ports (:5012–:5019) in one line; the port authority does not. Gate B is met for them through their code, C-02 and their app charters.

evidence.observation: 23 entries: 20 services · backup-job · shared · template; 8 with port_required = true
business 0 · life 0 · nexus 0 · platform 0 · search 0 · trust 0 · backup 0 · ai 1 · connection 1

findings.root_cause: Services were added after C-20 was last rewritten; check-drift checks only the services C-20 lists.
findings.technical_impact: No canonical statement of what those services own, which port they use, or who calls them.
findings.business_impact: Ownership questions (C-68) for eight services are answered from memory.
findings.recommendation: Extend C-20 to every deployed service (role, owner, port source, network) and make check-drift compare the service list itself.
acceptance_criteria: Every directory in tec-core-backend with a package.json and a Dockerfile appears in C-20
check-drift.py fails when one does not

remediation.note: The auditor's error: the search looked for 'tec-<name>', and C-20's table names services by their short name ('life', 'ai' …). C-20 lists all 20 services with their ports. What was real: check-drift.py's service list is typed by hand, so a new service would be invisible to it — it now fails on any service in code it does not list (shown firing by removing 'trust' from the list).
